clue.text: Delight at finding pasture in unpolluted environment

indicators.note: 'in' together with 'environment' says one word sits within the surroundings of another
an environment is what surrounds something, so the pasture word is enclosed by the unpolluted word

parts.note: unpolluted means pure, free of contamination
leas are meadows or pasture land, a poetic word much used in crosswords

explanation.surface: Someone takes delight in coming across a meadow in a clean, unspoilt landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'environment' works with 'in' as the container signal: the pasture word sits inside the unpolluted word. 'at finding' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Delight and pleasure are synonyms for enjoyment or gratification.

clue.text: Personal assistants hold little power, that's plain

indicators.note: 'hold' says the assistants enclose the power word

parts.note: PA is the abbreviation for personal assistant, so PAS for more than one
amp, short for ampere, is a unit of electrical current, a small measure of power

explanation.surface: Office helpers have no real clout, that's obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' seems to mean obvious, but it is a stretch of flat grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are the vast grassy plains of South America.

clue.text: Wiped out, as deer might well be

indicators.note: the letters of the words before it might well be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Deer could easily be wiped out by hunters.
explanation.definitionFit: Erased means rubbed out or obliterated, so wiped out.

clue.text: Most reasonable since returning home

indicators.note: 'returning' tells us the word for since is read backwards

parts.note: as can mean since, as in 'as it rained, we stayed in'
a nest is a home, especially a bird's

explanation.surface: Coming back home is the most sensible thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' applies only to the word for 'since', not to 'home'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanest means most rational, the superlative of sane, which matches most reasonable.

clue.text: Take ill swallowing stagnant water and he'll go to court

indicators.note: 'swallowing' tells us the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: to take something ill is to resent it
a pond is a small body of still water

explanation.surface: Someone takes offence on drinking pond water and decides to sue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take ill' suggests getting sick, but it means take offence, RESENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A respondent is a defendant, especially in a divorce or appeal case, who must answer in court.

clue.text: Look for quiet in a school

indicators.note: 'in' tells us the quiet letter is placed inside the school word

parts.note: a school of thought or belief is a sect
p (piano) is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a calm appearance at a school.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is the look or appearance of something, as in 'a pleasant aspect'.

clue.text: The sailing man keeps food in dry wrapping

indicators.note: 'in' with 'wrapping' says the food word goes inside the dry word
'wrapping' says the dry word is wrapped around the food word

parts.note: to sear is to scorch or dry up; sear is also an old spelling of sere, dry
fare is food, as in 'simple fare'

explanation.surface: A sailor stores provisions in waterproof packaging.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafarer is a sailor, someone who travels by sea.

clue.text: A European schoolboy must accept direction

indicators.note: 'must accept' says the schoolboy word takes the direction letter inside it

parts.note: an Etonian is a pupil at Eton College, the English public school
S, south, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A European pupil has to accept guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is a famous English boarding school, so its pupil is an ETONIAN; S goes after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An Estonian is a native of Estonia, a European country on the Baltic.

clue.text: Stand, strange to relate

indicators.note: 'strange' says the following letters are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: An odd thing to say aloud: someone takes a stand.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to put up with or tolerate it, as in 'I can't stand noise'.

clue.text: The parsimony of the average head!

parts.note: the mean is the average of a set of values
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the person in charge is a typically stingy boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' suggests a headteacher or boss, but here it is a geographical headland, NESS (as in Loch Ness or Orford Ness).
explanation.definitionFit: Parsimony is extreme reluctance to spend, which is stinginess.

clue.text: Palest possible colour

indicators.note: 'possible' suggests one possible rearrangement of the letters of the preceding word

explanation.surface: The faintest shade one could choose.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastel is a soft, pale shade of colour.

clue.text: Loathing for a certain form

parts.note: a version is one particular form of something, such as an edition of a text

explanation.surface: A strong dislike of a particular shape or format.
explanation.definitionFit: Aversion is strong dislike or hatred, a synonym of loathing.

clue.text: The way a guy points-right

parts.note: a guy is a man
N and E are compass points, north and east

explanation.surface: A man gestures to the right to show the route.
explanation.definitionFit: Manner means the way something is done, as in 'in this manner'.

clue.text: Sound about money-not above asset-stripping

indicators.note: 'about' says the sound word goes around the following pieces

parts.note: a ping is a short ringing sound
L stands for pound (libra), the British unit of money
under is the opposite of above

explanation.surface: A remark that a financier stripping assets is solvent but not lofty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'solvent', but it is a noise; 'about' wraps it round the money letter and the word for 'not above'.
explanation.definitionFit: Asset-stripping is taking a company's valuable parts for profit, a form of plundering or pillaging.

clue.text: Corrupting mature worker without hesitation

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of 'outside' places the hesitation sound on the outside of the worker, ahead of it

parts.note: mature means grown up, adult
er is the sound of hesitation in speech
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A grown employee who acts decisively is somehow a corrupting influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without hesitation' reads as 'promptly', but 'without' means outside: the hesitation sound sits just outside the worker.
explanation.definitionFit: An adulterant is a substance that debases or contaminates something, so as an adjective it describes a corrupting agent.

clue.text: A five inside stepped forward

indicators.note: 'inside' says the five letter is put within the stepped word

parts.note: danced means moved with steps
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A number five player came onto the pitch and moved up the field.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue reads 'few', an OCR slip for 'five' (V). 'stepped forward' reads as one phrase, but only 'forward' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Advanced can mean forward, as in a precocious child or a far-on stage of development.

clue.text: Making dope doubly popular is criminal!

indicators.note: 'doubly' says the dope word appears twice in succession

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Selling drugs that are twice as fashionable is a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' suggests drugs, but it is a fool, ASS, written twice.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a murderer, so a criminal.

clue.text: One's urge to appear liberal

indicators.note: the letters given need to appear in another form, a rearrangement

parts.note: the letters of one's are used, the apostrophe aside

explanation.surface: Someone's impulse to seem broad-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'One's' is part of the fodder: ONES plus URGE rearranges into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean open-handed or lavish in giving, the sense of generous.

clue.text: Making out many nice rings can be fake

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, crosswords' 'many'

indicators.note: the letters given could form a fake, a rearranged version of themselves

explanation.surface: Being able to tell that many pretty rings could be counterfeit.
explanation.definitionFit: Making out means perceiving or distinguishing, which is what discerning does.

clue.text: Regret split about exercise

indicators.note: 'about' says the split word goes around the exercise word

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone regrets tearing a muscle during a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: To repent is to feel sorry about something done, so to regret it.

clue.text: A mind quite — is a mind distress'd." Cowper (Retirement)

definitions.text: A mind quite — is a mind distress'd." Cowper (Retirement)

parts.words: A mind quite — is a mind distress'd." Cowper (Retirement)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from William Cowper's poem Retirement; the missing word describes an empty, unoccupied mind

explanation.surface: A line of Cowper's poetry with a word left out.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted line from Cowper's Retirement reads with this word, meaning empty or idle, filling the gap.

clue.text: Concerned with an engineer on a ship getting a break

parts.note: re means concerning or with reference to
CE is a civil engineer
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Something about a ship's engineer getting time off.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is a pause or break, as in a parliamentary recess.

clue.text: Moderates set a graduate back

parts.note: the clue word set is used as it stands
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Politically moderate people return a university graduate to their group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the whole run SET A BA, reading ABATES.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate is to lessen or diminish, so moderates (as a verb) means abates.

clue.text: Refuse to give a needlewoman time

parts.note: one who sews is a sewer (pronounced like 'sower')
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone declines to grant a seamstress more time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun (waste); SEWER here is someone who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewerage is waste matter carried by sewers, so it is refuse.

clue.text: Star actors maybe

indicators.note: 'maybe' says the letters of the word before it are perhaps rearranged

explanation.surface: Perhaps the leading actors in a show are stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Castor is a bright star in the constellation Gemini, one of the twins.

clue.text: A rage followed by depression due to a dog

indicators.note: 'followed by' places the depression word after what comes before

parts.note: ire is anger or rage
a dale is a valley, a depression in the land

explanation.surface: Fury and then low spirits caused by a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests low mood, but here it is a dip in the landscape, DALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a breed of large terrier dog from Yorkshire.

clue.text: The girl in the rose-garden is enchanted by it

indicators.note: 'in' says the name is concealed in the words that follow

explanation.surface: A girl in a rose garden is captivated by its beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across 'garDEN IS Enchanted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Denise is a girl's name.

clue.text: A soldier in a bad state worries

indicators.note: 'in' puts the soldier inside the rearranged letters
'bad' says the letters of a state are in a poor, disordered condition

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier in a terrible condition frets.

explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to disturb or trouble someone, so it means worries.
